name: capsule-react
description: ReAct loop coordinator. Stateless state machine for reasoning-and-action cycle. Part of Unicity AOS.
readmeExcerpt:
# astrid-capsule-react




**The ReAct loop coordinator for [Astrid OS](https://github.com/unicity-astrid/astrid).**

In the OS model, this capsule is the shell. It drives the reasoning-and-action cycle that makes an agent an agent: fetch context, think, act, observe, repeat.

## State machine

```text
Idle -> AwaitingIdentity -> AwaitingPromptBuild -> Streaming -> AwaitingTools -> Streaming -> ... -> Idle
```

The react loop contains no inference logic. It is pure control flow that coordinates five other capsules over the IPC event bus:

1. **Session** - fetch conversation history, persist turn results
2. **Identity** - build the system prompt from workspace config
3. **Prompt Builder** - merge plugin contributions into the final prompt
4. **Provider** (e.g. Anthropic) - stream LLM responses
5. **Tool Router** - dispatch tool calls and collect results

## What it does not do

This capsule does not call LLMs, execute tools, build prompts, or store messages. It orchestrates the capsules that do. Replacing this capsule with a different orchestration strategy (debate, MCTS, chain-of-verification) changes the agent's behaviour without touching any other capsule.

## Persistence

Ephemeral per-turn state is stored in the capsule KV store:
- `react.turn.{session_id}` - current turn state
- `react.req2sess.{request_id}` - request-to-session correlation
- `react.call2sess.{call_id}` - tool call-to-session correlation

This is control flow state, not conversation history. History lives in the session capsule.

## Development

```bash
rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --release
```

aiSummary.oneLiner: A stateless Rust ReAct loop coordinator serving as the core control flow for Astrid OS.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: astrid-capsule-react functions as a highly decoupled control-flow component that orchestrates the fundamental reasoning-and-action (ReAct) cycle for the Astrid OS environment. It acts purely as a state machine, meticulously coordinating the complex interplay between session history, prompt building, LLM streaming, and tool routing without executing any inference logic itself. By communicating exclusively over an IPC event bus, it drives the 'fetch context, think, act, observe' loop while keeping ephemeral state isolated in a fast KV store. This architectural design ensures that the core orchestration strategy can be radically modified or replaced without destabilizing other system capsules.
keyFeatures: Stateless state machine design: Manages complex transition phases (like AwaitingPromptBuild or Streaming) without permanently storing conversation data.
IPC event bus coordination: Communicates securely and asynchronously with five distinct system capsules to execute the full agent lifecycle.
Decoupled inference logic: Isolates control flow entirely from LLM execution, ensuring that prompt generation and tool execution remain separate concerns.
Ephemeral KV persistence: Stores crucial per-turn state and request-correlation data in a fast, temporary key-value store for rapid retrieval.
WebAssembly compilation target: Compiles strictly to the wasm32-unknown-unknown target, ensuring lightweight, portable execution across environments.

useCases.title: Modular Agent Architecture
useCases.description: Systems engineers utilize the capsule to orchestrate complex AI workflows where components like memory and tool execution are strictly physically isolated.

useCases.title: Orchestration Strategy Experimentation
useCases.description: AI researchers swap out this specific ReAct capsule with alternative strategies (like Monte Carlo Tree Search) without needing to rewrite the rest of the OS.

useCases.title: Secure Tool Routing
useCases.description: Security architects rely on the decoupled event bus design to ensure the reasoning engine cannot directly access or execute unauthorized system tools.

useCases.title: Cross-platform OS Deployment
useCases.description: Developers compile the capsule to WebAssembly to run the core agent control loop efficiently within browser environments or edge nodes.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: This component is designed for advanced systems engineers, AI researchers, and developers building modular, OS-level agent architectures. It requires deep knowledge of Rust, state machine design, and WebAssembly compilation targets.
